trials.name: EPOCH
trials.primary_endpoint: [Part I (Base Study)] Change From Baseline in the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale (ADAS-Cog) Score
trials.results_summary: The trial was terminated early for futility. Verubecestat did not improve cognitive or functional outcomes compared to placebo and was associated with accelerated hippocampal volume loss and adverse safety signals.

trials.name: APECS
trials.population: Prodromal Alzheimer's Disease, Amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment, Alzheimer's Disease
trials.primary_endpoint: Part 1 (Base Study). Least Squares Mean (LSM) Change From Baseline in Clinical Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) Score at Week 104
trials.results_summary: The trial in prodromal Alzheimer's disease was also terminated early for lack of efficacy. Verubecestat failed to improve clinical ratings on the CDR-SB and showed similar adverse effects on cognition and brain volume.

related_evidence.description: Publication of the Phase 2/3 EPOCH trial results showing lack of efficacy and increased adverse events in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.
Publication of the Phase 3 APECS trial results confirming futility and worsened cognitive/atrophy outcomes in prodromal Alzheimer's disease.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence decisively supports the document's central claims that the BACE inhibitor verubecestat failed to demonstrate efficacy and presented significant safety concerns. The Phase 2/3 EPOCH trial (NCT01739348) in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease was terminated early due to definitive futility on all cognitive and functional primary endpoints. This failure was completely replicated by the subsequent Phase 3 APECS trial (NCT01953601) in prodromal patients, which was similarly halted for lack of efficacy. Both trials confirmed a concerning class-effect paradox where BACE inhibition led to accelerated hippocampal volume loss and worsened cognitive metrics, leading to the complete discontinuation of the verubecestat program.
